newsitem.title: USA: MGE wheat falls on profit taking, hedge selling.
newsitem.headline: MGE wheat falls on profit taking, hedge selling.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures dropped Wednesday amid thin profit taking in the September and December positions, traders said.
One trader said there was a little bit of hedge selling in the May contract and farmers were pricing some deferred wheat.
Traders said Wednesday's action was a correction from Tuesday when MGE spring wheat closed higher.
"In new-crop months, there is a feeling that flooding in the Red River Valley region will not be as bad as people had originally anticipated," the trader said.
He noted that additional spring wheat business may be slow because the Canadians have been fairly aggressive sellers in the last few days.
"There is a feeling that Canadians will dominate spring wheat export sales until the new crop comes on," the trader said.
At 1008 CST, MGE May spring wheat futures were off 3-1/2 cents at $4.06 a bushel while the rest of the board was down 3-1/2 to 4-3/4 cents.
